title: Quiz: Red Shift and the Expanding Universe

options.text: The absorption of light by the atmosphere
The change in frequency or wavelength of a wave due to relative motion between source and observer
The splitting of white light into a spectrum
The bending of light around massive objects

questions.explanation: The Doppler effect is the change in frequency (or wavelength) of a wave caused by relative motion between the source and the observer. It applies to both sound waves (e.g. ambulance sirens) and light waves.

questions.stem: What happens to the wavelength of light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?

options.text: It disappears completely
It decreases (blue shift)
It increases (red shift)
It stays the same

questions.explanation: When a galaxy moves away from us, its light waves are stretched to longer wavelengths. This shifts the light towards the red end of the spectrum, which is called red shift.

questions.stem: What did Edwin Hubble discover about distant galaxies?

options.text: They are all stationary
They are all the same distance away
They are all moving away from us, with more distant galaxies receding faster
They are all moving towards us

questions.explanation: Hubble discovered that light from nearly all galaxies is red shifted, meaning they are moving away from us. Furthermore, more distant galaxies show greater red shift, indicating they recede faster. This led to Hubble's law: v = H0 x d.

questions.stem: What does Hubble's law (v = H0 x d) tell us?

options.text: The mass of a galaxy is proportional to its distance
The size of a galaxy depends on how far away it is
The recession velocity of a galaxy is directly proportional to its distance from us
The brightness of a galaxy is proportional to its speed

questions.explanation: Hubble's law states that the recession velocity of a galaxy is directly proportional to its distance from us. This means the further away a galaxy is, the faster it is moving away, providing evidence that the universe is expanding.

questions.stem: A spectral line normally at 500 nm is observed at 510 nm from a distant galaxy. What is the red shift?
questions.explanation: Red shift z = (change in wavelength) / (original wavelength) = (510 - 500) / 500 = 10 / 500 = 0.02. This tells us the galaxy is moving away from us.

questions.stem: Why is the expanding universe not expanding from a central point?

options.text: Because space itself is expanding, carrying galaxies with it, so every point sees all others receding
Because the universe is flat
Because galaxies are moving through space like rockets
Because only some galaxies are moving away

questions.explanation: Space itself is expanding, like dots on an inflating balloon. From any point, all other points appear to be receding. There is no centre to the expansion because the Big Bang happened everywhere, not at a single point.

questions.stem: What is the cosmic microwave background radiation?

options.text: Radiation from nearby stars in the Milky Way
The cooled remnant of radiation from the early universe, detected as microwaves from all directions
Radiation produced by modern radio transmitters
Radiation from the Sun reflected by the Moon

questions.explanation: The cosmic microwave background is uniform microwave radiation detected from all directions in space, corresponding to a temperature of about 2.7 K. It is the red-shifted afterglow of the hot, dense early universe, discovered by Penzias and Wilson in 1965.
